findings.rule: specs/requests/01-requests.md:126 requirement 19: "Every message writes a `RequestEvent` with `action = 'message_posted'` in the same transaction as the `RequestMessage` row, and updates `Request.lastActivityAt`."
findings.claim: the decline branch creates a RequestMessage without the message_posted RequestEvent that requirement 19 makes unconditional, so the audit mechanism is present at one of the two RequestMessage call sites and absent at the other

witness.detail: POST /api/organizations/{orgId}/requests/{id}/decline as the addressee with reason 'No budget'. requests.service.ts:522 writes the RequestMessage; the only events.record call in the block is the status_changed one at :548. Afterwards requestMessage.count({where:{requestId}}) === 1 but requestEvent.count({where:{requestId, action:'message_posted'}}) === 0. The identical body sent through POST .../messages does write the event (requests.service.ts:453). Requirement 25 makes the decline reason a RequestMessage 'posted in the same transaction', so requirement 19 applies to it; requirement 21 ('A message never appears in the history except as the fact that one was posted') makes the omission observable - the History panel of a declined request shows the status change and never records that the reason message exists. TC-01-INT-11 (apps/api/test/requests.spec.ts:658) queries only action:'status_changed', so nothing in the suite catches it.

findings.suggestedFix: After tx.requestMessage.create in the decline branch, call this.events.record(tx, { requestId, actorKind: 'member', actorMembershipId: caller.membershipId, action: 'message_posted', newLabel: caller.displayName }) - the same call postMessage makes at :453 - and extend TC-01-INT-11 to assert both events.

findings.rule: CLAUDE.md (Watch out for): "**Role values are in transition.** The database holds `admin` / `member`; the specs target `admin | manager | user | viewer`. New authorization code must handle both" - restated by specs/requests/01-requests.md:50: "Capability checks run against `normalizeRole()` (`packages/validation/src/roles.ts`), so the legacy `member` value maps to `user` and the matrix holds against today's data."
findings.claim: the new page passes the raw Membership.role into can(), which does not normalize, so a legacy `member` is treated as having no capabilities at all and loses controls the server grants them

witness.detail: An organization whose memberships still hold the legacy role `member`, which CLAUDE.md states is what the database holds. That member signs in; /api/me returns role: 'member' unnormalized (apps/api/src/members/me.controller.ts:39) and it reaches the client verbatim (session-context.tsx:33 types it `string`). At page.tsx:88, can('member' as Role, 'create-request') evaluates CAPABILITY_MATRIX['member'], which is undefined, so `?? false` returns false (packages/validation/src/index.ts:717). requests-new-btn is not rendered. The same account's POST /api/organizations/{orgId}/requests returns 201, because the service normalizes first (requests.service.ts:846). Requirement 1 withholds the control from `viewer` only. page.tsx:89's can(role,'list-assigned-projects') fails the same way, so the project filter and the modal's project picker are not drawn either. The repository already ships the normalizing helper for exactly this and uses it at Sidebar.tsx:120 and documents/page.tsx:114. No test catches it: e2e helpers.ts:164 types setMembershipRole to the four target values only, so `member` is never exercised.

findings.suggestedFix: Use hasCapability(session.role, 'CreateRequest') / hasCapability(session.role, 'ViewAllRequests') - which normalize internally (roles.ts:154) and are why the spec requires the capability in both unions - or normalize once with normalizeRole(session.role) before every can() in page.tsx and requests-badge-context.tsx. The detail page needs no change: its isAdmin test is role === 'admin', which is spelled identically in both vocabularies.

findings.rule: CLAUDE.md (Conventions that matter, Testing): "retiring a case is recorded in its spec as `- **Retired.**` naming what covers the rule now." Handoff task T9 names the file: files: ["apps/api/test/requests-page.spec.ts", "e2e/tests/requests-page.spec.ts", "specs/user-management/10-*.md"]
findings.claim: T9 was executed on its two test files and not on the spec it was reversing: spec 10 still states 403 for user and viewer where the shipped endpoint now answers 200, and a second case's retirement note is justified by that now-false rule

witness.detail: specs/user-management/10-organization-requests-page.md:270-278 - 'TC-10-INT-03: Requests page - forbidden for user/viewer ... Expected Result: 1-2. HTTP 403 with { "error": "forbidden" }'. apps/api/test/requests-page.spec.ts:368 now asserts expect(uRes.status).toBe(200) for the same call, because requests/01 requirement 37 reverses it. `git diff --name-only f06c7d8...HEAD -- specs/` is empty, so no spec file was touched at all. Worse, spec 10:297 retires an E2E case with '- **Retired.** Covered by TC-10-INT-03 (a user and a viewer are forbidden)' - a replacement rule that no longer exists, so the retired case's coverage claim is now unbacked. The handoff's own risk register (handoff.json:449-451) predicted this and prescribed the mitigation: 'record the retirement in specs/user-management/10 as `- **Retired.**` naming TC-01-INT-18 and TC-01-E2E-08'.

findings.suggestedFix: Mark TC-10-INT-03 in specs/user-management/10-organization-requests-page.md as `- **Retired.**` naming TC-01-INT-18 and TC-01-E2E-08 as what covers the rule now, and repair the retirement note at :297 so it points at the surviving rule rather than at TC-10-INT-03. Routed to `code` and not `spec` because requests/01 requirement 37 already authorizes the amendment in writing ('This amends the page-level `view-requests` gate of spec 10'); no human ruling is needed, only the bookkeeping the handoff assigned.

findings.rule: .claude/skills/code-review/SKILL.md sweep 8: "**A test nothing can break is a finding**: an assertion about a value nothing produces, a selector nothing renders, a query that resolves to the wrong element, a mechanism that throws before the assertion runs"
findings.claim: the closing assertion of the spec's designated badge regression witness cannot fail, so the half of requirement 44 that says the badge empties when the work is done is unproven

witness.detail: requests.spec.ts:551 reloads the page. The shell remounts with badgeCount initialised to 0 (requests-badge-context.tsx:39 useState(0)) and Sidebar.tsx:88 renders the badge only when badgeCount is truthy, so the node is absent before the GET /requests it depends on has resolved. toHaveCount(0) at :553 therefore passes on its first poll. The preceding anchor at :552 is sidebar-requests-link, which renders synchronously from the session and says nothing about the fetch. If the server returned waitingOnMe: 2 for two granted requests, or the client summed the wrong counters, this assertion would still pass. The spec calls this case 'the regression witness for the change proven absent at spec time'.

findings.suggestedFix: Anchor the final check on the response: await page.waitForResponse on the requests list before asserting, or assert a post-response node first (a row, or requests-empty-state), then toHaveCount(0). requests-page.spec.ts:182 shows the genuine shape - there the badge is showing '2' in the same DOM when the check begins.

findings.rule: .claude/skills/code-review/SKILL.md sweep 8: "**A test nothing can break is a finding**: ... a selector nothing renders ... or a mechanism that throws before the assertion runs"
findings.claim: the `user` half's vacation-section assertion cannot fail, leaving the UI half of AC-2 and AC-3 unproven at the only level that can observe it

witness.detail: openRequestsPage (requests.spec.ts:157-163) waits only for requests-page, the outer div rendered before any fetch (page.tsx:287). requests-vacation-section is rendered only from data.vacation (page.tsx:439), so it is absent at mount and toHaveCount(0) at :473 passes on the first poll while the list request is still in flight - the assertion holds even if the server wrongly returned a vacation block to a `user`. The admin half at :468 is anchored by toBeVisible and is sound. Narrowed from the shard's claim: the requests-scope-toggle assertion at :474 is fine, because canScopeAll is a synchronous render from the session (page.tsx:89) and does not depend on the response.

findings.suggestedFix: Before the absence assertion, wait for something only the response can draw - await expect(page.getByTestId('requests-empty-state')).toBeVisible() for that user, or a seeded row - then assert requests-vacation-section is absent.

findings.rule: specs/requests/01-requests.md:1035 TC-01-INT-13 Steps: "Create a request with `neededBy` = tomorrow, then read it as an account whose timezone makes that date past." - and .claude/skills/code-review/SKILL.md (Clearing an item): "When a rule is unconditional as written and the code gives a reason it should not apply, that is a contradiction between the code and the spec. Report it, with `"target": "spec"`, and let a human rule on it. Never settle it yourself by preferring the code."
findings.claim: the case as written is unsatisfiable, so no implementation can execute its steps; the implementation substitutes two different routes and argues the exception in a code comment

witness.detail: The widest UTC offset spread is 26 hours (UTC-12 to UTC+14), so two readers' calendar dates differ by at most one day and the furthest-ahead reader's today is an upper bound on every reader's today. A neededBy strictly after the creator's today is therefore after every reader's today and cannot be past for any of them. apps/api/test/requests.spec.ts:702 accordingly does not create with neededBy = tomorrow; it uses the western reader's today plus a PATCH to '2020-01-01', and explains the substitution in a comment at :697-701. AC-8 is still reached by those two routes, so this is a spec defect rather than missing coverage - but the spec's numbered steps are executed nowhere, and a code comment is not a source that can clear them.

findings.suggestedFix: Amend TC-01-INT-13's steps to the two routes that are actually reachable and that the spec itself already describes - the timezone boundary day of edge case 10, and a neededBy moved into the past after creation (requirement 8: 'it may become past afterwards, which is what makes a request overdue') - so the case and the spec agree. Routed to spec because no implementation satisfies the steps as written; sending it to code would loop the implementer forever.

findings.rule: specs/requests/01-requests.md:181 requirement 36: "It is flagged `assigneeInactive` on read and appears under the reassignment filter." contradicted by specs/requests/01-requests.md:204 requirement 42: "Filters: `type` (`all` | `access` | `question` | `vacation`), `status` (...), `projectId`, and a free-text `q` matched against `title` case-insensitively."
findings.claim: two numbered requirements contradict: 36 names a reassignment filter that 42's exhaustive list does not contain, that no test id is named for, and that no test case exercises

witness.detail: Requirement 42 enumerates the filters exhaustively and names four. The Required data-testid list (specs/requests/01-requests.md:709-712) names requests-type-filter and requests-status-filter and no fifth control. parseRequestScope/parseRequestStatusQuery/parseRequestTypeQuery (packages/validation/src/requests.ts:450-469) accept nothing else, and page.tsx:327-365 renders exactly the four. The implementable half of requirement 36 - the flag on read, nothing cancelled, the banner, the reassign control - is implemented and covered by TC-01-INT-17 and TC-01-E2E-09. Both review shards reached this independently.

findings.suggestedFix: Resolve in the spec: either drop the 'and appears under the reassignment filter' clause from requirement 36, or add the filter to requirement 42 with a test id and a case. Do not settle it in code - a requirement with no artefact is invisible to every other sweep.

findings.rule: specs/requests/01-requests.md:1274 TC-01-E2E-13 Steps: "Apply a status filter that matches nothing, then clear it on an account with no requests at all." Selectors: "requests-status-filter, requests-type-filter, requests-empty-state"

findings.rule: specs/requests/01-requests.md:692: "Anything missing goes into the design system and is recorded in a DS-gaps table, not improvised here." - restating CLAUDE.md: "Anything missing goes *into* the design system and is recorded in that spec's \"DS gaps\" table, never improvised per screen."
findings.claim: the spec demands a DS-gaps table and contains none, while the change ships five primitives that have no @ds export

witness.detail: grep -i 'ds gap' over specs/requests/01-requests.md finds the demand at :692 and no table anywhere in the file. The change ships three token-carrying native textareas (NewRequestModal:318, [requestId]/page.tsx:365, DeclineRequestModal:127), a native date input (NewRequestModal:406), a hand-rolled skeleton (page.tsx:685) and a hand-rolled empty state (page.tsx:403). handoff.json:440-446 carries the five rows that were meant to land in that table. findings.rule: specs/requests/01-requests.md Data Model, RequestEvent: "`oldLabel` / `newLabel` - Display-name snapshots at write time, so the trail survives a removed member." No rule states the actor fallback, so this is judgement
findings.claim: the actor fallback conflates two different people: on an assignee_changed row newLabel is the new addressee, not the actor

witness.detail: RequestHistory.tsx:20 reads `const actor = event.actor.displayName ?? event.newLabel ?? 'Former member'`, and :29-31 renders `${actor} reassigned it from ${oldLabel} to ${newLabel}`. An event whose actorMembershipId was SetNull therefore renders 'Robin Ops reassigned it from Pat Member to Robin Ops', naming the new addressee as the person who performed the reassignment. Reachable only after a hard delete of the membership, since removal is a soft delete - which is why this is a note.

findings.suggestedFix: Fall back to 'Former member' directly for the actor, and use newLabel only where the event's own semantics define it as the actor (message_posted's author snapshot, requirement 20).

findings.rule: CLAUDE.md (Conventions that matter, Design system): "**No hardcoded colors or sizes** - use tokens (`var(--sp-8)`, `var(--fs-14)`, `var(--text-muted)`)."
findings.claim: raw pixel layout sizes are introduced: maxWidth 820 (page.tsx:303 and [requestId]/page.tsx:201), minWidth 170 three times and 200 once, the skeleton's block dimensions, Modal width 520/440, and `padding: 'var(--sp-4) 12px'` mixing a token with a literal

witness.detail: CLAUDE.md forbids hardcoded sizes without qualification and page.tsx:303 sets maxWidth: 820 literally. Every colour, spacing and typography value in the diff is a token; only layout widths and the input-chrome pixels are literal, and those copy shipped precedent byte-for-byte (members/[memberId]/RejectRequestModal.tsx:198, time-tracking/page.tsx:278). Filed as a note rather than a blocker because it is the repository-wide spelling rather than this diff's regression, and the only conforming fix is a design-system change this spec does not own.

findings.suggestedFix: Add a container-width token to the design system and record the gap in the table F15 asks for, or have a human rule that layout widths sit outside the rule and say so there.

findings.rule: no written rule covers a read failure on the detail screen - the spec's UI Description error row is scoped to the list ('Error (list)'), so this is judgement
findings.claim: any detail-load failure other than 404 is swallowed, leaving a screen with no message, no retry and nothing distinguishing it from a slow load

witness.detail: GET /api/organizations/{orgId}/requests/{id} answers 500, or the fetch throws. detail stays null and notFound stays false, so /org/{orgId}/requests/{id} renders request-detail-page containing only the back link, indefinitely; a reload is the only recovery and nothing on screen says so. The list screen was given a banner and a retry for exactly this case.

findings.suggestedFix: Track a load error alongside notFound and render the same banner plus retry shape the list uses, with REQUEST_MESSAGES.genericError.
